threatFindings.threat: Theft self-kill: when 2 or more teams that route their captured zombies through [5D13h] (m050, b01d, e1p4, FixedToggle, Synthesis) are present, base B almost never survives (our B writes [5D13h] last, so their captures run our zombie_entry at phases 2000h/3400h inside B's band).
threatFindings.evidence: r53y6 base B score 0.000 (m050 x2), 0.044 (e1p4 x2), 0.081 (FixedToggle x2), 0.125 (Synthesis x2), 0.144 (b01d x2); dz1uy heterogeneous m050+Synthesis base B 0.040 (12/12 cohorts <= 0.15). Screen S base: sstrong-1 (b01d+e1p4) B 0.02, sstrong-5 (m050+Synthesis) B 0.00. Single router (q2hkx): B 0.34-0.44, no collapse. Moving only the two zombie phases restores B (zph 0.42-0.59; E2 0.35-0.61). Extends B063 (b01d+e1p4+segfault) to every router type and to a heterogeneous pair.
threatFindings.impact: Team points per battle in affected cohorts: +0.20 (2 copies, 5 routers) to +0.27 (m050+Synthesis) with zph. Prevalence: 15.5% of 3-team cohorts drawn from the strong pool (2024 final + counters + peers) contain >= 2 routers and 62% contain >= 1 (fields.mjs partition). The archived 2025/2024/2023 pools contain no [5D13h] router (B063 hookscan); Registered_Winners routes via [9769h] (single router). Estimated base cost ~0.03 points/battle on the strong group (0.155 x ~0.22), consistent with zph's confirmed strong-group gain +0.027 (mc03n); ~0 on the plain 2025 field.

threatFindings.threat: Mechanism of the router-case collapse is the B059 startup collision (stolen zombies' first anchor/trail on B's pending startup code)
threatFindings.evidence: Contradicted in magnitude by the startup Monte Carlo (startup-mc.mjs): per captured zombie the geometric chance to hit B's pending code is ~1.1% (zom20a path) / ~0.3% (b/d path), so even 6 stolen zombies give < 10% of battles, while B is lost in ~95% of router-pair battles. The cause is tied to the zombie phase (zph and E2 both fix it) and to the number of stolen zombies (single router: no collapse). Likely: many same-phase zombie streams on B's lattice inside B's band (crossfire / anchor merge, cf. A016 m-model). Not traced: trace jobs cannot use custom cohorts.
threatFindings.impact: The fix does not depend on the mechanism: every out-of-band zombie phase tested (5Ch/70h, 68h/94h, 9Ch/B0h and L63 in screen cohort sstrong-1) removes the collapse; 5Ch/70h (zph) gives the largest team gain.

threatFindings.threat: Startup self-writes in ordinary battles (own/partner hook-cell writes, own anchors and first trails, captured-zombie first anchors/trails)
threatFindings.evidence: Monte Carlo over random loads with 1024-byte separation and exact rev0 instruction timing (startup-mc.mjs, 200k samples): some member's pending code is hit in 2.82% of battles (B 2.02%, A 0.82%); captured-zombie anchors/trails ~1.5% (Za trail->B 0.86%, Za anchor->B 0.23%, Zbd trail->B 0.23%, zombies->A ~0.2%); six hook-cell x warrior combinations ~0.19% each (~1.15% total); A/B own anchors and first trails < 0.1%. Zombie phases 5Ch/70h (zph) or 68h/94h (E2) cut the total to 1.46-1.47% (remainder = cell writes + zombie trails over A). Base trace pkj3o observed 3 zombie startup kills + 1 cell self-hit in 160 battles (model expects ~2.3 + ~1.8).
threatFindings.impact: Captured-zombie part ~0.005/battle in ordinary 2025 cohorts (fixed by zph); hook-cell part <= ~0.004/battle (1.15% x <= 0.35 points), below screen resolution; no fix proposed (a guard costs startup instructions, which A001/A003 found timing-sensitive).

threatFindings.threat: Hook-cell and zombie-trail writes corrupt B's zombie_entry before a late zombie uses it (capture lost, not a death)
threatFindings.evidence: Monte Carlo only: 1.6% of battles in base, 0.6% with zph/E2 phases (remaining part = the three fixed cell writes).

recommendation: Include zph (B only, zero bytes, B sha e85a4bf6...) in the next combination/base candidate. The self-harm it removes is large and now verified across all five [5D13h]-router teams and a realistic heterogeneous pair: base B is almost always lost when two routers are present (B 0.00-0.14/battle); zph gives +0.20 [0.14,0.26] (r53y6) and +0.27 [0.18,0.35] (dz1uy); this situation occurs in ~15% of strong-pool cohorts (expected ~+0.03/battle on strong, matching the confirmed +0.027). General cost measured earlier is small (confirm mc03n 2025 -0.003, nozombie +0.001). Prefer zph over A016 E2 for this threat (E2 +0.07 on the same cohorts). Remaining startup self-harm (fixed hook-cell writes, ~1.15% of battles) is below screen resolution; do not spend jobs on it. Not a stand-alone promotion: zph alone failed the pooled gate (mc03n lo -0.012); combine it with B054 fix2steal and A003 C1 (fix2steal edits zombie_entry, so port only the two mov bp immediates).
